name: Cofer Black

summary.text: J. Cofer Black is a former CIA officer who directed the Director of Central Intelligence's Counterterrorist Center (CTC) from 1999 until May 2002, including at the time of the September 11, 2001 attacks, and later served as the State Department's Coordinator for Counterterrorism. He testified before the Joint Inquiry of the congressional intelligence committees in September 2002 and before the 9/11 Commission in April 2004.

openQuestions: Black's later role as vice chairman of Blackwater USA (2005–2008) was not confirmed by any source found in this session and is left out.

The site places Black among those who 'withheld intelligence from the FBI' on Hazmi and Mihdhar. No source found attributes that decision to Black personally; the DOJ Inspector General's 2004/2006 review (oig.justice.gov/special/s0606) attributes the non-notification to CIA personnel without naming him. Unsupported as to Black individually.
A 2005 Los Angeles Times report, relayed by a partisan blog, said Black's 2002 testimony about an FBI memo was misleading; it was not verified and is left out.
